definition: Recovering an image from corrupted, compressed, or undersampled measurements — spanning denoising, deblurring, and inverse problems solved with learned priors.
details: Recovering an image from corrupted, compressed, or undersampled measurements — spanning denoising, deblurring, and inverse problems solved with learned priors.

explainer.lead: Image reconstruction recovers an image from corrupted, compressed or undersampled measurements. It spans denoising, deblurring and inverse problems solved with learned priors.

tiers.eli5: Like rebuilding a clear picture from a smudged or incomplete copy of it.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers frame recovery as an inverse problem and supply learned priors; a common pitfall is that undersampled measurements can be filled with detail that was never measured.

explainer.example: Recovering an image from undersampled measurements using a learned prior.
